All six faces of a cube are painted with different colors – violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow and orange.

On the opposite side of the green page is the purple page.

The blue page is between the green and purple pages.

The orange page is adjacent to the yellow page.

Indigo page is adjacent to orange page.

If the green page is at the bottom, what is the color of the upper page?
questions.solution:
**Given:** All six faces of a cube are painted with different colors – violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow and orange.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/72084078d16d4fbb6dbe7cf94f3ab7e3693f56efd24f6bf41709f3f095cc3660.png] 

1) The green page is at the bottom

2) On the opposite side of the green page is the purple page.

As green page is at the bottom and is opposite to the purple page, therefore purple page will be at the top of the cube.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fad14ee490265a45f99ae08bd91a223b8b61a3f8caabf52f0a2e7a99918f28e7.png] 

3) The orange page is adjacent to the yellow page.

4) Indigo page is adjacent to orange page.

As direction of orange page with respect to either yellow page or Indigo page is not given yet, therefore yellow page and indigo page can be either side of orange page.

As, top and bottom of the cube are already painted, therefore the 3 sides out of 4 sides will be painted in the order of "**Indigo page / Yellow page - Orange page - Indigo page / Yellow page**".

As direction of orange page with respect to either top page or bottom page is not given yet, therefore orange page can be at the either sides of the cube.

Case 1)

3) The blue page is between the green and purple pages.

The blue page can be painted at one of the either 4 sides of the cube left as all the 4 sides are between top and bottom.

Case 1)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dfd2de97a52ad229e34088d112e05f4e4ccf5b3b3cdd1e9a934591d66d1dca5f.png] 

Case 2)

Thus, in both cases, purple is the color of the upper page.

Hence, **"Option 2"** is the correct answer.

A statement in this question and the two conclusions related to them are given in the form of i and ii, assuming the word of the statement as true, it is to decide which conclusions relate to the statement is logical and logical and logical.

**Statement:** X company has temporarily stopped manufacturing its products.

**Conclusion:**

i) Company X has the possibility of resuming production.

ii) Company X should arrange an advertising campaign so that the product reaches people better.

Select the correct option from the following.

(A) Only conclusions i is logical.

(B) The only conclusion ii is logical.

(C) The conclusions i or ii are logical.

(D) Neither conclusion nor ii is rational.

(E) i and ii both conclusions are logical.
questions.solution:
**Given Statement:**

X company has temporarily stopped manufacturing its products.

**Conclusions:**

I. Company X has the possibility of resuming production - **Follows** (Because the statement says the stoppage is temporary, implying a possibility of resumption.)

II. Company X should arrange an advertising campaign so that the product reaches people better - **Does not follow** (Because the statement only mentions the temporary stop in manufacturing and doesn't provide information about the need for an advertising campaign.)

So, Only **conclusion I** is logical.

Hence, the correct answer is ***'Option 2'.***

questions.question:
Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it.

First row: 7, 9, 39

Second row:4, 8, 28

Third row: 6, 7,?

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the number into its constituent digits. For example, 13 - Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

**(First number × 3) + (Second number × 2) = Third number**

First row: 7, 9, 39 → (7** × 3**) **+** (9 **× 2**) = 21 + 18 = 39

Second row: 4, 8, 28 → (4 × 3) + (8 × 2) = 12 + 16 = 28

**Third row: 6, 7,? **→ (6 × 3) + (7 × 2) = 18 + 14 = **32**

Hence, **32** is the correct answer.

questions.question: Five years ago, Vinay's age was (1)/(3) of the age of Vikas and now Vinay's age is 17 years. The present age of Vikas is

Five years ago, Vinay's age was (1)/(3) of the age of Vikas -

Vinay - 5 = (1)/(3) (Vikas - 5 )

Now Vinay's age is 17 years.

Vinay = 17 putting above equation we get -

Vikas - 5 = 36

Vikas = 36 + 5

Vikas = 41

The present age of Vikas is 41 year.

Hence, **"41 year"** is the correct answer.

questions.question: Krishna gave 1/9 of his savings to his son, 3/4 of the remaining to his first daughter, and the rest to his second daughter. If the first daughter received Rs. 880 more than the second one, how much did the son get?
questions.solution:
Krishna gave 1/9 of his savings to his son, 3/4 of the remaining to his first daughter, and the rest to his second daughter.

Let the total savings of Krishna be Rs. a

Savings Krishna gave to his son = a/9

Remaining amount = a - a/9 = 8a/9

Savings Krishna gave to his first daughter = (8a/9)(3/4)= 2a/3

Savings Krishna gave to his second daughter = 8a/9 - 2a/3 = 2a/9

If the first daughter received Rs. 880 more than the second one

According to question:

2a/ 3 - 2a/9 = 880

⇒ (6a - 2a)/9 = 880

⇒ 4a/9 = 880

⇒ a = (880 × 9)/4

⇒ a = 1980

Amount of money the son got = a/9 = 1980/9 = 220

Hence, ‘**220**’ is the correct answer.

questions.question:
The admission ticket for an Art Gallery bears a password which is changed after every clock hour based on set of words Chosen for each day. The following is an illustration of the code and steps of rearrangement for subsequent clock hours.

The Time is 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. Day’s first password:

**First Batch** – 9 a.m. to 10 a.m. is not ready cloth simple harmony burning

**Second Batch** – 10 a.m. to 11 a.m. ready not is cloth burning harmony simple

**Third Batch** – 11 a.m. to 12 noon cloth is not ready simple harmony burning

**Fourth Batch** – 12 noon to 1 p.m. not is cloth ready burning harmony simple

**Fifth Batch **– 1 p.m. to 2 p.m. ready cloth is not simple harmony burning and so on.

If the password for 11 a.m. to 12 noon was –“soap shy miss pen yet the she”, what was the password for the First Batch?

options.text: pen miss shy soap she the yet
shy miss pen soap yet the she
soap pen miss shy she the yet
miss shy soap pen she the yet

questions.solution:
The given arrangement is as under :

1) In the first step, the first three and the last three letters are written in reverse order.

2) Then, the first four and the last three letters are written in reverse order.

3) The process is repeated to obtain successive output steps. 

**For the Third batch:** soap shy miss pen yet the she

**Second batch: **pen miss shy soap she the yet

**First batch:** shy miss pen soap yet the she

Hence,** "shy miss pen soap yet the she" **is the correct answer.

questions.question: Mishti's birthday is on Thursday 27th April. On what day of the week will be Aradhya's Birthday in the same year, if Aradhya was born on 20th October?
questions.solution:
Misthi’s birthday = 27th April → Thursday

Aradhya’s birthday = 20th October

Number of days between 28th April to 20th October:

Days left in April = 3

May = 31

June = 30

July = 31

August = 31

September = 30

October = 20

Total days = 176

Number of odd days = 176/7 → 1

So, Aradhya’s birthday will be on Thursday + 1 day = Friday.

Hence, the answer is Friday.

questions.question: In a class of 100 students, 24 students score more marks than Sharmistha whereas 18 students score lesser marks than Amit. How many students score lesser marks than Sharmistha but more marks than Amit?
questions.solution:
From the given information:

Total number of students in a class = 100

Students with marks more than Sharmistha = 24

Students with marks less than Amit = 18 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f8e5d34e554cf6f0154cd01d0317c999810a58eb808de46cda58f366b7932d19.png] 

Total = 24 + 18 = 42

Now we have to find out the number of students who score lesser marks than Sharmistha but more marks than Amit: 

100 - 42 - 2 (Sharmistha & Amit) ⇒ **100 - 44 = 56**

**Hence the correct answer is option 3)**

questions.question:
In a certain code language,

'A ÷ B means 'A is the wife of B',

'A - B' means 'A is the father of B',

'A × B' means 'B is the mother of A',

'A $ B' means 'A is the sister of B',

'A + B' means B is the daughter of A'.

Based on this information, how is P related to M if 'P ÷ Q - R + S × T $ M'?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5e7db211f11195c72136a85e4990d1cb984eacaeda88edbc0f9d73ed73569ece.png] 

Given:

In a certain code language,

'A ÷ B means 'A is the wife of B',

'A - B' means 'A is the father of B',

**'A × B' means 'B is the mother of A',**

'A $ B' means 'A is the sister of B',

**'A + B' means B is the daughter of A'.**

Let us first decode the given symbols and then draw a family tree:

 
 

 A is
 ** B is**
 
 

 Symbol
 ÷ 
 -
 $ 
 × 
 +
 
 

 Meaning
 Wife
 Father
 Sister
 Mother
 Daughter
 
 

 ** of B**
 ** of A**
 
 

 

On checking:** 'P ÷ Q - R + S × T $ M' **

**1) 'P ÷ Q' **

'P ÷ Q' means 'P is the wife of Q'. 

**2) 'Q - R'**

'Q - R' means 'Q is the father of R'. 

**3) 'R + S** 

'R + S'means S is the daughter of R.

**4) 'S × T'**

'S × T' means T is the mother of S.

**5) 'T $ M'**

'T $ M' means T is the sister of M. 

 
• Thus, the following family tree can be drawn:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5e921927f8ed50b6bcd032f59d37fd9c0dbda4bd307cb2d55bbef702642f7eb0.png] 

 
• Clearly,** P is Sister's husband's mother of M.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Sister's husband's mother".**

questions.question:
Read the given instructions carefully and answer the question:

Point B is 7 km to the west of point A.

Point C is 12 km to the south of point E.

Point A is 5 km to the east of point C.

Point D is 8 km to the north of point C.

Point G is 6 km to the west of point D.

Point H is 14 km to the south of point G.

If Shubham is standing 6 km to the east of point H and takes 1 hour to complete 6 km distance then in what possible time he would reach point E, if taken the shortest route?
questions.solution:
**Given Statements:**

1) Point B is 7 km to the west of Point A,

2) Point C is 12 km to the south of point E,

3) Point A is 5 km to the east of Point C,

4) Point D is 8 km to the north of point C,

5) Point G is 6 km to the west of point D,

6) Point H is 14 km to the south of point G,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4c47125100e1a3cae6046c4845960a791f610d94dc1f08edb43bde0b774073f2.png] 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a74a0cb68dde727604d39eab7c168f7af7647622b2d8255a2dddaab9332c22f9.png] 

 

Now, Shubham turns towards East 6km in 1 hour,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e2624e8a90d148e4e13c047635b2897b59a888c82bcef643dc9e26badab409f9.png] 

Finally, the total time and distance required to Shubham to point E is:

Distance = 14 + 4 = 18 km,

Time = 6 km = 1 hour = 60 Minutes,

Thus, total time = 60 × 3 = 180 Minutes(3 hours),

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1".**

**Two** persons stand between Q and U
